Complete Lifetime Value Sales & Client Experience Playbook

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION & PHILOSOPHY
Purpose of This Playbook
This comprehensive document exists to transform your entire team into confident, ethical revenue generators who prioritize client outcomes above all else. Every interaction is an opportunity to serve, educate, and build lifetime relationships that benefit both your clients and your practice.
The Luxora Sales Philosophy
Sales is service. Service is sales.
At Luxora, we reject the notion that sales is separate from care. When you educate properly, recommend appropriately, and guide confidently, you ARE selling — and that's a good thing.
Core Beliefs:
Every client deserves a complete treatment plan, not just a single service
Education eliminates buyer's remorse and increases satisfaction
Commitment (packages/memberships) produces better clinical outcomes
Confidence in your recommendations builds trust
Systems create consistency, consistency creates culture
Lifetime value beats transactional thinking every time
What Makes Luxora Different
We don't believe in:
High-pressure tactics
Pushing services clients don't need
Commission-driven recommendations
One-size-fits-all approaches
Leaving revenue on the table through timidity
We do believe in:
Confident, educational conversations
Comprehensive treatment planning
Value-based positioning
Strategic upselling tied to outcomes
Creating predictable, recurring revenue through memberships
SECTION 2: ROLE-SPECIFIC CAPABILITIES MATRIX
Who Can Do What: Complete Authority Guide
*Estheticians can consult on skincare and facial treatments only **Estheticians recommend within their scope (facials, skincare, body treatments)
SECTION 3: SITUATIONAL SALES SCENARIOS
SITUATION 1: First-Time Client Inquiry (Phone)
Scenario: Potential client calls asking about Botox pricing
Who Handles: Front Desk
Objectives:
Avoid pricing in isolation
Position value before cost
Secure consultation
Plant package/membership seed
Complete Script Flow:
Client: "Hi, how much is Botox?"
Front Desk: "Great question! I'm so glad you called. My name is [Name]. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with?"
Client: "[Name]"
Front Desk: "Wonderful, [Name]. I love that you're thinking about this. Before I talk numbers, can I ask — is this your first time considering neurotoxin treatments, or have you had Botox before?"
Client Response A: "First time"
Front Desk: "Perfect! So here's what I recommend: Botox is typically priced per unit, and everyone needs a different amount based on their goals and muscle strength. Rather than throw a random number at you, let's get you in for a complimentary consultation with one of our injectors. They'll assess exactly what you need, show you what's possible, and give you precise pricing. Most clients find this way more helpful than a phone quote. Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?"
Client Response B: "I've had it before"
Front Desk: "Awesome! So you know how it works. Our pricing is $12 per unit, and most clients use between 20-60 units depending on the areas they treat. That said, we also offer packages and a membership that brings your cost down significantly — especially if you're maintaining this regularly. Would you like to come in and speak with an injector about a long-term plan, or would you prefer to just book a single treatment?"
Key Teaching Points:
Never give pricing without context
Always offer consultation for new clients
For returning clients, mention packages immediately
Use assumptive language ("when" not "if")
SITUATION 2: Client Books Single Treatment Online
Scenario: Client self-schedules a single laser hair removal session via website
Who Handles: Front Desk (confirmation call) → Consultant (day-of)
Objectives:
Educate on treatment series requirements
Position package before arrival
Set expectation for consultation upsell
Front Desk Confirmation Call Script:
Front Desk: "Hi [Name], this is [Your Name] from [Practice]. I'm calling to confirm your laser hair removal appointment on [Date] at [Time]. Do you have a quick second?"
Client: "Yes"
Front Desk: "Perfect! I just want to make sure you have the right expectations. Laser hair removal isn't a one-and-done treatment — it typically takes 6-8 sessions for permanent reduction. Most of our clients purchase a package upfront because it saves money and ensures they complete the full series. When you come in, your consultant will go over the options with you. Sound good?"
Client: "Okay, yes"
Front Desk: "Great! We'll see you [Day] at [Time]. Looking forward to meeting you!"
Day-of Consultant Script:
Consultant: "Hi [Name]! Welcome. I see you're here for laser hair removal. Have you done this before, or is this your first time?"
Client: "First time"
Consultant: "Perfect. So here's what you need to know: one session will reduce some hair, but you won't see permanent results. Hair grows in cycles, so we need to catch it multiple times. The gold standard is 6-8 treatments, spaced 4-6 weeks apart. We have a few options:
Single session: $350
Package of 6: $1,800 (saves $300)
Package of 8: $2,400 (saves $400 and ensures complete results)
Most clients go with the 6 or 8 because they want this done right. Which makes more sense for your goals?"
Key Teaching Points:
Educate before they arrive
Frame packages as the standard, not an upsell
Use savings language
Give clear options with recommendation
SITUATION 3: Client Hesitant About Package Pricing
Scenario: Client wants results but resists package investment
Who Handles: Consultant, Esthetician, Nurse, or Injector (whoever is presenting)
Objectives:
Reframe from cost to value
Break down cost-per-result
Offer payment plans
Compare to doing nothing
Complete Objection Handling Script:
Client: "That's more than I wanted to spend"
You: "I totally understand — I want to make sure you're comfortable. Can I ask, what were you thinking investment-wise?"
Client: "I was hoping to just do one and see"
You: "That makes sense, and you absolutely can. Here's what I want you to know: when clients do one treatment, they see some improvement, but it's temporary. Then they come back six months later and we're starting over. The clients who get the results they actually want are the ones who commit to the full series upfront. So it's less about spending more — it's about actually solving the problem versus just renting a solution. Does that make sense?"
Client: "Yeah, but I still don't know if I can afford it right now"
You: "Totally fair. We do offer payment plans — you can spread this over [X] months, which brings it down to about [Y] per month. That's less than most people spend on coffee. And honestly, if this is important to you, isn't it worth financing a real solution rather than wasting money on things that don't work?"
Alternative Approach (Budget-Conscious):
You: "I hear you. Let me ask — what's your timeline? Are you trying to see results for a specific event, or is this more of a general goal?"
Client: "I just want to look better"
You: "Got it. So here's another option: we have a membership that spreads the cost out monthly and gets you access to multiple services at a lower rate. A lot of clients find that easier to budget for. Want me to walk you through it?"
Key Teaching Points:
Never argue, always empathize first
Reframe cost as investment in results
Offer payment plans immediately
Compare to cost of NOT solving the problem
SITUATION 4: Retail Recommendation During Facial
Scenario: Esthetician performing facial on client with visible hyperpigmentation
Who Handles: Esthetician
Objectives:
Tie retail to treatment outcomes
Position as essential, not optional
Recommend full routine, not single product
Overcome "I'll think about it"
Treatment Room Script:
During Treatment:
Esthetician: "So while we're working on your skin today, I'm noticing some hyperpigmentation around your cheeks and forehead. Is that something you've been trying to address?"
Client: "Yeah, I've tried a few things but nothing really works"
Esthetician: "That makes sense — hyperpigmentation is stubborn. The good news is, what we're doing in-clinic today will help, but if we don't support it at home, the results won't last. I'm going to recommend a few products that actually work. Sound good?"
Client: "Sure"
At End of Treatment:
Esthetician: "Okay, so here's what your skin needs. I'm recommending three things:
Vitamin C serum in the morning — this brightens and prevents new spots
Retinol at night — this accelerates cell turnover and fades existing spots
SPF 50 daily — because UV exposure will undo everything
These three together are what all my clients with hyperpigmentation use, and they see results in about 4-6 weeks. The investment is about $180 total, and these will last you 3-4 months. Do you want to start with the full routine or just pick one?"
Client: "That's expensive. Can I just get the Vitamin C?"
Esthetician: "You can, but here's the thing — if you only do one, you won't see the results you want. It's like going to the gym once a week and expecting a six-pack. These products work together. If budget is the concern, I'd rather you start with the retinol and SPF, because those will give you more visible improvement. But ideally, all three."
Client: "Let me think about it"
Esthetician: "Of course! But can I be honest? Every client who says 'let me think about it' either forgets, or buys something random at Target that doesn't work, and then we're back here having the same conversation in three months. You're already investing in facials — let's make sure that investment actually pays off. If you get these today, I'll follow up with you in a month and we'll see what's working. Deal?"
Key Teaching Points:
Diagnose the problem during treatment
Recommend a complete system, not a single product
Tie to treatment they're already paying for
Overcome objections with truth and urgency
SITUATION 5: Client Wants "Just Botox" But Needs More
Scenario: Client books Botox but would benefit from filler, skin tightening, or full-face plan
Who Handles: Injector or Provider
Objectives:
Assess true goals vs. stated request
Educate on comprehensive approach
Present tiered options
Close on highest appropriate tier
Complete Consultation Script:
Injector: "Hi [Name], good to see you! So I see you're here for Botox today. Tell me — what are you hoping to improve?"
Client: "I just want to get rid of these forehead lines"
Injector: "Got it. And if we could wave a magic wand and make you look exactly how you want, what else would you change?"
Client: "Honestly, I hate these smile lines and my eyes look tired"
Injector: "Okay, so it's not just your forehead — it's also volume loss and overall tired appearance. Here's the thing: Botox will absolutely help your forehead, but it won't touch the smile lines or the tired eyes. For that, we need filler. Let me show you what I mean."
[Uses mirror to show anatomy]
Injector: "See how when you smile, these lines deepen? That's not a muscle issue — that's volume loss. Botox can't fix that. And your under-eyes? That's hollowing. If we add a little filler here, here, and here, you'll look refreshed and rested. Does that make sense?"
Client: "Yeah, but how much is filler?"
Injector: "Great question. Let me give you three options:
Option 1: Botox Only
Forehead, glabella, crow's feet
40 units at $12/unit = $480
This addresses lines, but not volume or tired appearance
Option 2: Botox + Strategic Filler
Same Botox areas
1 syringe filler in smile lines
Total: $1,180
This addresses lines and one volume concern
Option 3: Full-Face Rejuvenation (What I Recommend)
Botox in all areas
2 syringes filler (smile lines + under-eyes)
Total: $1,880
This is the complete solution that addresses everything you mentioned
Most clients in your situation choose Option 3 because it solves the whole problem at once. Which feels right to you?"
Client: "I don't know if I want to spend that much today"
Injector: "Totally understand. Here's what I'd suggest: let's do Option 2 today, and then we can add the under-eye filler in 2-3 weeks once you see how much better you already feel. How's that sound?"
Key Teaching Points:
Use discovery questions to uncover full needs
Educate with mirror/visual tools
Present tiered options with clear recommendation
Don't back down from full plan, but offer staged approach

TEMPLATE 1: Discovery to Close (Consultations)
Step 1: Build Rapport
"Thanks for coming in today! Tell me a little about yourself — what do you do?"

SECTION 5: UPSELL STRATEGIES BY SERVICE CATEGORY
CATEGORY 1: Injectable Services (Botox, Dysport, Filler)
Who Can Upsell: Injectors, Providers, Nurses, Consultants
Primary Upsell Opportunities:
A. Single Area → Multiple Areas
Scenario: Client books Botox for forehead only
Script: "Most clients who do forehead also do glabella and crow's feet because treating all three creates a more balanced, natural look. If we only do forehead, you might notice the other areas more. Want to add those today?"

Scenario: Client in chair for Botox
Script: "Botox handles movement lines beautifully. But I'm noticing some volume loss here and here. If we add just one syringe of filler, you'll look 5 years younger instead of just smoother. Want to do both?"
C. Single Treatment → Package
Scenario: Client paying per visit
Script: "You're coming every 3-4 months anyway. If you buy a package of 4 treatments, you save $[X] and you're guaranteed pricing for the year. Should we lock that in today?"
D. Pay-Per-Visit → Membership
Scenario: Loyal injectable client
Script: "You spend about $[X] per year on injectables. Our VIP membership is $[Y]/month and includes a credit, discounts, and priority booking. Over the year, you'd save $[Z]. Want me to switch you over?"
CATEGORY 2: Laser & Energy-Based Treatments
Who Can Upsell: Consultants, Estheticians, Nurses, Providers
Primary Upsell Opportunities:

Scenario: Client books one laser facial
Script: "Laser treatments are cumulative — one session gives you a glow, but a series of 3-6 actually corrects [concern]. We have a package of 3 for $[X], which saves you $[Y]. Most clients start with that. Should we go ahead?"

Script: "Our signature facial is great for maintenance, but if you want to actually correct [acne/aging/pigmentation], I'd recommend our [advanced facial]. It includes [benefits] and most clients see dramatic improvement. Want to upgrade?"

Script: "I can add [dermaplaning/LED/high-frequency] for just $[X] more. It takes 10 minutes and doubles your results today. Want me to include it?"

Lack of urgency
Unclear value

     5	---
     6	
     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `pandoc` or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	### Converting .doc to .docx
    22	
    23	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    24	
    25	```bash
    26	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    27	```
    28	
    29	### Reading Content
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	# Text extraction with tracked changes
    33	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    34	
    35	# Raw XML access
    36	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    37	```
    38	
    39	### Converting to Images
    40	
    41	```bash
    42	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    43	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    44	```
    45	
    46	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    47	
    48	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    49	
    50	```bash
    51	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    52	```
    53	
    54	---
    55	
    56	## Creating New Documents
    57	
    58	Generate .docx files with JavaScript, then validate. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    59	
    60	### Setup
    61	```javascript
    62	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    63	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    64	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,
    65	        VerticalAlign, PageNumber, PageBreak } = require('docx');
    66	
    67	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    68	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    69	```
    70	
    71	### Validation
    72	After creating the file, validate it. If validation fails, unpack, fix the XML, and repack.
    73	```bash
    74	python scripts/office/validate.py doc.docx
    75	```
    76	
    77	### Page Size
    78	
    79	```javascript
    80	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    81	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    82	sections: [{
    83	  properties: {
    84	    page: {
    85	      size: {
    86	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    87	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    88	      },
    89	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
    90	    }
    91	  },
    92	  children: [/* content */]
    93	}]
    94	```
    95	
    96	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
    97	
    98	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
    99	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
   100	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
   101	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
   102	
   103	**Landscape orientation:** docx-js swaps width/height internally, so pass portrait dimensions and let it handle the swap:
   104	```javascript
   105	size: {
   106	  width: 12240,   // Pass SHORT edge as width
   107	  height: 15840,  // Pass LONG edge as height
   108	  orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE  // docx-js swaps them in the XML
   109	},
   110	// Content width = 15840 - left margin - right margin (uses the long edge)
   111	```
   112	
   113	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)
   114	
   115	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.
   116	
   117	```javascript
   118	const doc = new Document({
   119	  styles: {
   120	    default: { document: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 24 } } }, // 12pt default
   121	    paragraphStyles: [
   122	      // IMPORTANT: Use exact IDs to override built-in styles
   123	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   124	        run: { size: 32, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   125	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 240 }, outlineLevel: 0 } }, // outlineLevel required for TOC
   126	      { id: "Heading2", name: "Heading 2", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   127	        run: { size: 28, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   128	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 180, after: 180 }, outlineLevel: 1 } },
   129	    ]
   130	  },
   131	  sections: [{
   132	    children: [
   133	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   134	    ]
   135	  }]
   136	});
   137	```
   138	
   139	### Lists (NEVER use unicode bullets)
   140	
   141	```javascript
   142	// ❌ WRONG - never manually insert bullet characters
   143	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("• Item")] })  // BAD

   293	### Step 1: Unpack
   294	```bash
   295	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
   296	```
   297	Extracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`“` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.
   298	
   299	### Step 2: Edit XML
   300	
   301	Edit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.
   302	
   303	**Use "Claude" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.
   304	
   305	**Use the Edit tool directly for string replacement. Do not write Python scripts.** Scripts introduce unnecessary complexity. The Edit tool shows exactly what is being replaced.
   306	
   307	**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:
   308	```xml
   309	<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->
   310	<w:t>Here’s a quote: “Hello”</w:t>

   312	| Entity | Character |
   313	|--------|-----------|
   314	| `‘` | ‘ (left single) |
   315	| `’` | ’ (right single / apostrophe) |
   316	| `“` | “ (left double) |
   317	| `”` | ” (right double) |
   318

   320	```bash
   321	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Comment text with & and ’"
   322	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 "Reply text" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0
   323	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Text" --author "Custom Author"  # custom author name
   324	```
   325	Then add markers to document.xml (see Comments in XML Reference).
   326	
   327	### Step 3: Pack
   328	```bash
   329	python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
   330	```
   331	Validates with auto-repair, condenses XML, and creates DOCX. Use `--validate false` to skip.
   332	
   333	**Auto-repair will fix:**
   334	- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)
   335	- Missing `xml:space="preserve"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace
   336	
   337	**Auto-repair won't fix:**
   338	- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations
   339	
   340	### Common Pitfalls
   341	
   342	- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.
   343	- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.
   344	
   345	---
   346	
   347	## XML Reference
   348	
   349	### Schema Compliance
   350	
   351	- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last
   352	- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces
   353	- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)
   354	
   355	### Tracked Changes
   356	
   357	**Insertion:**
   358	```xml
   359	<w:ins w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   360	  <w:r><w:t>inserted text</w:t></w:r>
   361	</w:ins>
   362	```
   363	
   364	**Deletion:**
   365	```xml
   366	<w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   367	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   368	</w:del>
   369	```
   370	
   371	**Inside `<w:del>`**: Use `<w:delText>` instead of `<w:t>`, and `<w:delInstrText>` instead of `<w:instrText>`.
   372	
   373	**Minimal edits** - only mark what changes:
   374	```xml
   375	<!-- Change "30 days" to "60 days" -->
   376	<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>
   377	<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   378	  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>
   379	</w:del>
   380	<w:ins w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   381	  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>
   382	</w:ins>
   383	<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>
   384	```
   385	
   386	**Deleting entire paragraphs/list items** - when removing ALL content from a paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted so it merges with the next paragraph. Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:
   387	```xml
   388	<w:p>
   389	  <w:pPr>
   390	    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->
   391	    <w:rPr>
   392	      <w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
   393	    </w:rPr>
   394	  </w:pPr>
   395	  <w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   396	    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>
   397	  </w:del>
   398	</w:p>
   399	```

   401	
   402	**Rejecting another author's insertion** - nest deletion inside their insertion:
   403	```xml
   404	<w:ins w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   405	  <w:del w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   406	    <w:r><w:delText>their inserted text</w:delText></w:r>
   407	  </w:del>
   408	</w:ins>
   409	```
   410	
   411	**Restoring another author's deletion** - add insertion after (don't modify their deletion):
   412	```xml
   413	<w:del w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   414	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   415	</w:del>
   416	<w:ins w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   417	  <w:r><w:t>deleted text</w:t></w:r>
   418	</w:ins>
   419	```

   422	
   423	After running `comment.py` (see Step 2), add markers to document.xml. For replies, use `--parent` flag and nest markers inside the parent's.

   427	```xml

   429	<w:commentRangeStart w:id="0"/>

   431	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted</w:delText></w:r>
   432	</w:del>
   433	<w:r><w:t> more text</w:t></w:r>
   434	<w:commentRangeEnd w:id="0"/>
   435	<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="CommentReference"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id="0"/></w:r>
   436

   439	  <w:commentRangeStart w:id="1"/>
   440	  <w:r><w:t>text</w:t></w:r>
   441	  <w:commentRangeEnd w:id="1"/>
   442	<w:commentRangeEnd w:id="0"/>

   463	    <a:graphic>

   468	      </a:graphicData>
   469	    </a:graphic>
   470	  </wp:inline>
   471	</w:drawing>
   472	```
